newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: More to be done on Australia inflation - Evans.
newsitem.headline: More to be done on Australia inflation - Evans.

text.p: Australian Treasury Secretary Ted Evans said on Thursday there was more that could be done structurally to further improve Australia's inflation and growth performances.
"There is much that can be done in a structural sense to further improve both our inflation and growth performances and the trade-off between the two," Evans said in a speech to business economists.
"The substantial improvement in public sector saving now underway will ease the external constraint -- in fact it is already doing so," he said.
Evans said Australia's "superior" inflation performance had yet to be fully reflected in financial markets.

"While interest differentials have narrowed, Australian rates remain above those in the U.S. across the spectrum suggesting less than full confidence that our inflation performance will be sustained. Time will correct that," he said.
Evans said that since March 1993, Australia's cumulative annual average inflation had not exceeded 2.5 percent.

"There is an interesting question here of the extent to which these favourable inflation outcomes, both here and in the U.S. have reflected the fact that the forecasts which formed part of the policy-making framework were rather pessimistic concerning domestic inflationary pressures -- the alternative explanation being exogenous (and largely unpredictable) external influences on the exchange rate," he said.
The government forecast underlying inflation at two percent in year average terms in the year to June 30, 1998 from 1.25 percent in 1996/97.
The Reserve Bank of Australia aims to keep underlying inflation between two and three percent over the course of a business cycle.
Evans said the government's introduction of a tax rebate on personal contributions to superannuation and on the income from saving complemented focus on public sector saving.
